description: We’re a team of curious, hands-on builders who love exploring new things and learning by doing. Our background is in software development and AI, and we enjoy turning ideas into working apps, even when the topic is completely new to us. Space is new territory for most of us, which is exactly why we’re excited: we’re eager to dive in, research, experiment and learn as we go. We work well together, share ideas openly and aren’t afraid to try bold approaches.
summary: Orbitopia is a free, bilingual (English and French) web game that turns real NASA space-weather data into a junior astronaut mission trainer for children aged 7 to 12. Kids run a Moon or Mars base for seven days, and every day is a real day of the Sun from NASA’s DONKI database, fetched live with a saved backup for offline classrooms. Each morning they share out limited solar power between air, plants, radiation shields and exploration. At night, the real particle storm recorded by NASA is compared with their shield. Nova, a talking space cat, explains the problem in a short story first, reads everything aloud, accepts voice commands and answers questions with NASA sources. Every science star is a real NASA discovery. Astronauts on Artemis missions will face solar storms with limited power, and Orbitopia lets children experience those real decisions, even if they can’t read or type yet. It’s live at orbitopia.earth.
details:
What it does
Orbitopia is a free, bilingual (English and French) web game for children aged 7 to 12. Kids run a Moon or Mars base for seven days, and every day is a real day of the Sun from NASA’s DONKI space-weather database. It starts with a short animated story told by Nova, our talking space cat. The story explains why astronauts beyond Earth’s magnetic shield need power for air and protection from solar particle storms. Then children make the same kind of decisions a real crew would.

How it works
Each morning the solar panels give a few power bolts (5 on the Moon, 4 on Mars). Kids spend them on air (1 bolt makes 1 air), plants (1 bolt makes 2 air the next day), shields (2 bolts add one layer) or exploring (2 bolts and 1 air win a science star). Leftover bolts charge the battery, because at night (or “shadow time” at the Moon’s south pole) the heaters need power.

At night the real Sun arrives. The game takes that day’s biggest flare and whether NASA recorded a solar energetic particle (SEP) event. It turns them into a storm strength from 0 to 4 and compares it with the player’s shield. A flare without particles is just a “big flash”, so kids learn the difference. Kids can open the real data card for each day: flare class, particle storm time and CME speed.

The game fetches the last 7 days live from DONKI and falls back to five archived real weeks offline, such as the May 2024 superstorm. On Mars, messages take 4 to 22 minutes, so forecasts can be fuzzy unless kids build a radiation sensor modelled on NASA’s HERA on Orion. Every science star is a real NASA discovery card (LCROSS water ice, an LRO lunar cave, Perseverance’s ancient lake, Phoenix ice and more). Fact cards use OSDR RadLab ISS radiation data and OSDR space-biology studies.

Benefits

  • No reading or typing needed. Nova reads everything aloud, kids can tap or say commands like “two shields”, and “Ask Nova” answers 22 questions with NASA sources.
  • Every number is traceable to a NASA source.
  • Works offline after the first visit and installs as an app.
  • Free, no accounts, no tracking: settings stay on the device.
  • Lessons come from the child’s own choices: the end screen gives three lessons from their week, and an impact story links them to real Artemis planning.

What we hope to achieve
We want children to understand space weather and resource planning by doing, not just reading. Next, we hope to test Orbitopia in Mauritian classrooms, add Mauritian Creole and other languages, add a teacher dashboard, and add new missions such as the ISS and Lunar Gateway.

Tools and technologies

  • Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript (no framework).
  • A Progressive Web App (service worker and manifest).
  • The Web Speech API for voice output and speech recognition.
  • All characters and scenes drawn as SVG in code.
  • NASA DONKI (FLR, SEP and CME analysis), OSDR RadLab and the OSDR search API.
  • A Google Colab notebook to verify the data, and a Node.js balance simulation (200 games per strategy).
  • Playwright automated tests.
  • Hosting on GitHub Pages at orbitopia.earth.
